what: Defect 28 -- ownership of every harvested corpse, established by DIRECT SWEEP rather than by waiting for the race. Written 2026-07-29 at the P3.6 exit work.
method: SWEEP A (own scene at own teardown): every test's own fixture target checked under the deep invariants BEFORE its fixtures tear down, recording every I11 it holds. 518 collected, 18 I11-holding scenes, ALL of them in their own accepted baseline.

SWEEP B (every quiescent point): floorplanner.design.verify.fault_profile wrapped -- the one funnel verify/rebase/_verify_or_report all reach -- so every check of every scene is sampled, not just teardowns. 53 I11 observations, 12 distinct pairs, NO 'Kitchen'/'Pan' among them.

SWEEP C (force the leak): _commit_if_changed() -- the exact call the leaked QTimer makes -- invoked on EVERY live MainWindow after EVERY test, with windows tagged by their creating test. 0 reports: a stale window's walk is silent, because every I11 in a stale scene is in that scene's own baseline.

RE-HARVEST: 10 DEEP runs on the unfixed tree with dumps kept. 4 red, 14 dumps, and the four 20-room corpses carry their FULL documents -- which is what finally identified the owner, the reduced evidence file having kept only a summary.
PICK CENSUS: the owner test's party-wall pick walked exhaustively, 59 candidates, under two corner-move rules.

why_the_victim_varies.claim_withdrawn: 'the race picks the victim' -- there is no race in the choice.
why_the_victim_varies.mechanism: The test picks its party wall with next(w for w in win.scene.items() if ...). QGraphicsScene item order is not stable across processes, so the pick varies per run, and with it which corner moves and which rooms overlap.
why_the_victim_varies.rate: 18 of 59 candidate picks (31%) produce an I11 -- consistent with the 4-in-10 red DEEP runs measured on the unfixed tree.

root_cause.statement: The test hand-rolls a corner move and re-points the moved vertex for the party wall's TWO rooms only (`for r in (a, b)`). Any THIRD room whose outline holds that same corner keeps the old vertex and is left behind, so its region no longer agrees with the walls -- and where the geometry allows, it overlaps a neighbour.
root_cause.contrast_with_the_app: Both app corner-movers collect their holders from the geometry and re-point every one: `_DragVertex` (walls.py, the drag) carries `ends` and `edges`, and `GroupItem._corner_records` (items.py, bake and rotation) records every wall end and every outline edge on the corner.
root_cause.receipt: Re-pointing EVERY room holding the corner: 0 of 59 picks produce an I11, against 18 of 59 under the test's current rule.

not_established: That an equivalent APP gesture can strand a holder. A synthetic endpoint drag was attempted over 38 multi-room corners and moved the corner in NONE of them -- the mouse path did not drive that branch headlessly, so the run reported '0 stranded' vacuously. That reading is discarded rather than quoted: the app is neither cleared nor accused here.
That DEEP's green/red has been meaningless throughout (ruling 5's bound, unchanged). The observed instances remain P3.6's.
